title: The Story of Prince Bihzad
summary: Bakhtiyar recounted the history of Prince Bihzad of Azerbaijan:
full_text:
Bakhtiyar recounted the history of Prince Bihzad of Azerbaijan:

'Prince Bihzad was a youth of fiery valor, peerless skill with the scimitar, and boundless impatience. When an invading army of nomads crossed the northern frontier, the venerable commander of the royal forces counseled: "Prince, the nomads are swift in the open plain, but their supplies are meager; let us hold the mountain passes for seven days, and hunger will force them to retreat without a battle."

Bihzad scoffed at the veteran’s advice: "Shall we cower behind rocks like frightened foxes? A true champion charges the enemy without waiting for the sun to rise!"

Deaf to all counsel, Bihzad sounded the charge, galloped into the narrow defile at the head of five thousand horsemen, and fell squarely into a disguised pit-trap prepared by the invaders!

His army was scattered, four thousand brave soldiers fell in the ambush, and Bihzad was dragged from his horse, wounded and captured.

For three years, the proud prince labored as a captive in the northern steppes, herding shaggy horses in the snow, reflecting every bitter day upon his reckless impatience that had destroyed five thousand innocent companions.

When he was finally ransomed by his father, Bihzad was a transformed man: his fiery pride had been burned away, replaced by profound humility, strategic patience, and reverence for wise counsel.

When he ascended the throne, he never issued a military order without consulting his council of elders, ruling in peace for forty years as one of the wisest monarchs of the Caucasus.'
moral: Youthful impatience that ignores experienced counsel leads to defeat; humility rebuilds the kingdom.
